headline.definition: Production-weighted mean of the panel yield anomalies over the crop seasons with a usable weather-implied estimate (at least half the window run, standard error under 40 points, positive leave-one-year-out skill over the trend-only baseline). The index-implied figure is the paper's medium-scenario change aggregated over exactly the same seasons with the same weights. A mixture of crops weighted by tonnes, not a global food-supply estimate.

scenario.note: CPC September 2026 outlook quantiles, divided by 1.178 to the relative index; 2015-16 monthly shape

refresh.summary: Yields for Brazil, Argentina and six European countries now run to 2024-2025 from the national statistical agencies on the same reporting units, and the ENSO responses are refitted on them. Weather and the ENSO outlook are those of the 6 October issue.
changes: Tier-2 yields extended past the released Hultgren et al. (2025) panels with agency series on the same units: IBGE municipal maize and soybean (Brazil, to 2025), MAGyP departmental maize (Argentina, to 2025), Eurostat and Destatis maize (France, Spain, Austria, Belgium, Italy, Germany, to 2024); NASS extensions of US maize, soybean and sorghum as before.
Every ENSO response (country panel, state, unit) refitted on the extended series, so the Brazilian, Argentine and European fits now include the 2015-16 and 2023-24 events.

Subnational series ending before 2010 (China's county series end 2003; US and European series without an agency extension end 2003-2008) no longer carry a 2026-27 expectation; where a country and crop has only such series, the national FAOSTAT series to 2024 is used instead.
The tier-2 source is labelled hultgren rather than gmfd: the GMFD weather in those panels is not used, only their units and yields.
Series keep their database ids across the rebuild; new series take new ids.
Weather to 30 September (temperature source to 5 October), September ENSO observations and the 10 September outlook are unchanged from the 6 October issue.

coverage.definition: Production denominators include series with a fitted ENSO response, after source priority: HarvestStat, Hultgren, then national FAOSTAT. Missing responses are excluded rather than assigned zero impact.
